entries.clue: Stone found in bad pastry – not part of standard run (3-5)

indicatorNotes.found in: the stone is found inside the pastry

blocks.note: food gone bad has gone off
a pie is a pastry dish; it holds the stone
st = stone, the unit of weight

annotation.surface: A diner bites on a stone baked into a bad pastry.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue: everything before it is wordplay, and 'standard run' means a groomed ski run, not a jog or a print run.
annotation.definitionFit: Off-piste skiing happens away from the marked, groomed runs.

entries.clue: Cool down number two distributor in trouble (3)

blocks.note: to cool someone by wafting air at them
in the saying, trouble arrives when muck hits this and it sprays the mess everywhere

annotation.surface: An instruction to calm a deputy who is spreading trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number two' is a childish word for excrement, so the second definition is the saying 'when the shit hits the fan', dressed up politely.
annotation.definitionFit: A fan cools you down, and in the saying it is what scatters the mess when things go wrong.

entries.clue: Father starts preaching about Tibet’s esoteric religions (5)

indicatorNotes.starts: take the start of each following word

blocks.note: the first letters of the five words

annotation.surface: A priest begins a sermon on the mystical faiths of Tibet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Father' reads as a priest doing the preaching, but it is the definition: pater is Latin for father, and old-fashioned British slang for one.
annotation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father and a jokey old British word for one's dad.

entries.clue: Makes purchases when inebriated? They’ll be so dirty (4-6)

indicatorNotes.when: joins the two halves: shops, when oiled

annotation.surface: A drunk goes on a spending spree and ends up grubby.
annotation.walkthrough: Oiled is British slang for drunk. The question mark flags that the wordplay is read literally as someone who shops while oiled.
annotation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods have got grubby or worn from being on display in a shop.

entries.clue: Native elements in Nazareth nicely hidden (6)

indicatorNotes.elements in: the answer is made of parts of the next words
indicatorNotes.hidden: the answer is concealed in the words

annotation.surface: Local things are neatly concealed in Nazareth.
annotation.walkthrough: The indicator is split around its fodder, with 'elements in' before and 'hidden' after.
annotation.definitionFit: Ethnic means belonging to a people by birth or origin, much as native does.

entries.clue: I request silence during plot slip-up (6)

indicatorNotes.during: I and SH come in the middle of the plot

blocks.note: to plot is to map, and a plot is a map

annotation.surface: Someone shushes the audience during a plot twist that goes wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: Plot here is a map or chart, not a story line.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a small accident or blunder.

entries.clue: Section of Bremen University that deals with consumer choice (4)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a descriptive phrase for the thing, 'what deals with consumer choice'

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section of the next words

annotation.surface: A department of a German university studies consumer behaviour.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an economics faculty; the consumer is really a diner choosing from a menu.
annotation.definitionFit: A menu sets out the choices a customer can make.

entries.clue: Figure first possessed by a kind of spark (9)

indicatorNotes.possessed by: first is held inside the spark

annotation.surface: A figure is caught up in the first flash of inspiration.
annotation.walkthrough: IST is 1ST with the digit read as the letter I, a standard trick.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: figure in its numerical sense, a single piece of counted data.

entries.clue: It changes text to cure actor rambling (11)

indicatorNotes.rambling: the letters wander out of order

annotation.surface: Some tool edits a script to stop an actor going off on tangents.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder is everything between the definition and the indicator, 'to' included.
annotation.definitionFit: Autocorrect is the phone or computer feature that alters what you type.

entries.clue: Combination hits in boxing results in very short count (3,3)

blocks.note: a jab followed at once by a cross, two punches in quick succession
a count that stops at the second number

annotation.surface: A boxer's combination ends with the opponent down for barely a count.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxing surface makes 'count' look like the referee's count; it is just counting to two.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are literal: the boxing term for a two-punch combination, and the shortest count past one.

entries.clue: Women’s group eager to host northern prince (3,5)

indicatorNotes.to host: eager holds the northern prince inside it

blocks.note: a hearty appetite is an eager one

annotation.surface: A women's club is keen to welcome a royal from the north.
annotation.walkthrough: A hen party is the British name for a bride's night out with her friends before the wedding.
annotation.definitionFit: A hen party is a gathering of women, usually the bride-to-be's friends.

entries.clue: Arrogant British cut short broadcast (9)

blocks.note: CUT with its end cut off

annotation.surface: An arrogant Briton's broadcast is taken off air early.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' looks like a single instruction to trim British; in fact cut is itself the word that gets shortened.
annotation.definitionFit: Hubristic means showing hubris, excessive pride or arrogance.

entries.clue: Leading composer slipped up, losing right to be covered (11)

indicatorNotes.losing: to lose something is to be left without it, so ERRED is left without one R

blocks.note: a team that is up is leading
Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets
R = right; removed from ERRED to leave ERED

annotation.surface: A leading composer made a mistake and got a bad review.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading composer' looks like one phrase for a famous musician, but 'Leading' works alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Upholstered furniture is covered with padding and fabric.

entries.clue: Put forward idea for sports ground (5)

blocks.note: to propose, as a salesman does
the field for football or cricket

annotation.surface: Someone proposes a scheme for a new stadium.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a pitch is the playing field for football, rugby or cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: You pitch an idea to sell it, and a pitch is the ground games are played on.

entries.clue: Spied broken wire – that’s disgraceful (10)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters are broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: A spy is caught snooping on a cut wire, which is shameful.
annotation.walkthrough: Only part of the fodder is printed: wire must first become CABLE before the letters are mixed.
annotation.definitionFit: Despicable means deserving contempt, disgraceful.

entries.clue: Occasionally forgot duo’s name for this little character (6)

indicatorNotes.Occasionally: occasionally means now and then, so only some letters are used: every other one

blocks.note: F-R-O-D-O: the odd letters of forgot duo
Frodo names one of these creatures: the definition asks what kind of character he is

annotation.surface: Someone keeps forgetting the name of a double act's small sidekick.
annotation.walkthrough: The alternate letters do not spell the answer; they spell FRODO, and the clue then asks what Frodo is the name of.
annotation.definitionFit: Hobbits are Tolkien's small folk, and Frodo Baggins is the best known.

entries.clue: Benefit cuts for remote regions in the US (9)

blocks.note: to dock pay is to cut it

annotation.surface: Welfare cuts hit the far-flung parts of America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Benefit cuts' reads as one phrase about welfare, and British readers know 'benefits' as state welfare payments.
annotation.definitionFit: The boondocks is American slang for remote backcountry.

entries.clue: In drink, lieutenant is very loud singer (6)

indicatorNotes.In: the lieutenant goes in the drink

annotation.surface: A drunken officer turns out to be a very loud singer.
annotation.walkthrough: A belter is a singer who belts songs out at full volume.
annotation.definitionFit: To belt out a song is to sing it loudly, so a belter is a loud singer.

entries.clue: Assistant abandoned waste outlet cleaner in Dublin, he’s a fool (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is 'fool', qualified as Irish usage by 'in Dublin'

blocks.note: loo paper cleans up at the loo
PA = personal assistant, taken out of LOO PAPER

annotation.surface: An Irish cleaner's helper walks off the job, and he is called a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: Loo is British for toilet. 'Waste outlet cleaner' sounds like a drain unblocker, but it is the paper.
annotation.definitionFit: In Irish slang a looper is a crazy or foolish person.

entries.clue: First nation warrior is a bit erratic sounding (6)

indicatorNotes.sounding: the answer sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: patchy = erratic, uneven; 'a patchy' is the phrase said aloud

annotation.surface: A warrior of a native people behaves somewhat unpredictably.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit erratic' has to be turned into 'a patchy' before it is said aloud.
annotation.definitionFit: The Apache are a Native American people, famed as warriors.

entries.clue: Become keen on second opinion although it lacks weight (4,2)

indicatorNotes.lacks: to lack something is to be without it, so the word goes without its W

blocks.note: a take is an opinion, and two is the second
W = weight, the letter taken out

annotation.surface: Someone warms to a second opinion even though it carries little weight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take two' is a second take; losing W leaves the phrasal verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To take to something is to start liking it.

entries.clue: Musical composition incorporates core elements of Goethe and Auden (5)

indicatorNotes.core elements of: take the middle letters of each name

annotation.surface: A piece of music draws on the heart of Goethe's and Auden's poetry.
annotation.walkthrough: Goethe has an even number of letters, so its core is two letters; Auden's is three.
annotation.definitionFit: An étude is a short musical study, written to practise a technique.

entries.clue: Doctor sat in cafe entrance (9)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: A doctor sits in a café doorway.
annotation.walkthrough: Entrance is the verb, stressed on the second syllable, not the doorway the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to hold them spellbound, to fascinate them.

entries.clue: Musicians include individual piece in sacred text (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the piece goes inside the sacred text

annotation.surface: A band adds a solo to a setting of scripture.
annotation.walkthrough: A nonet is a group of nine players, or the piece written for them.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by group size: any ensemble of nine players is a nonet.

entries.clue: Mass chubby priest cut (4)

indicatorNotes.cut: to cut something is to remove it, so the priest is removed from chubby

blocks.note: P = priest, the letter taken out

annotation.surface: A tubby priest cuts short the Mass.
annotation.walkthrough: Mass sits next to priest to suggest a church service; it is a lump, a shapeless mass.
annotation.definitionFit: A lump is a solid mass with no particular shape.

entries.clue: Male friend in US picked up firm promotional material (8)

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: bro, American slang for a brother or buddy

annotation.surface: An American buddy lands some advertising work for his company.
annotation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company to go with the promotional material; it is the adjective, sure.
annotation.definitionFit: A brochure is a booklet advertising a product or service.

entries.clue: Pop group, by covering single, gets millions (5,1)

annotation.surface: A band covering someone else's single makes millions.
annotation.walkthrough: The music surface makes 'covering' and 'single' look like a cover version of a record. Boney M were a 1970s disco group.
annotation.definitionFit: Boney M were a disco group with hits such as Rivers of Babylon.

entries.clue: Finally try tofu cream – it’s delicious (3)

indicatorNotes.Finally: take the final letter of each word

annotation.surface: A diner finally tries tofu cream and declares it tasty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like it belongs to the surface's 'at last I tried it'; it applies to every word, not just one.
annotation.definitionFit: Yum is what you say when something tastes delicious.

entries.clue: It makes sense to link supplement to drink … (4,2)

annotation.definitionNote: 'it adds up' = it makes sense; the answer is the verb phrase

blocks.note: to supplement is to add to

annotation.surface: A health tip: taking a supplement with a drink is sensible.
annotation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue, but this clue works alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: when a story adds up its figures tally, so it hangs together.

entries.clue: … eventually it will provide extra income? (8)

blocks.note: given enough time; in the end
hours worked beyond the normal day are paid on top of wages

annotation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the supplement will pay off in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as two words, over time means eventually; as one word, it is the extra hours that earn extra pay.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: read as two words it means eventually; as one it is the paid extra hours.
